blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Distributed fiber-optic sensing (DFOS) technologies such as Distributed Acoustic Sensing (DAS) generate continuous, high-resolution spatio-temporal data at rates exceeding hundreds of megabytes per second, creating severe challenges for real-time storage and transmission. While neural compression methods can achieve strong rate-distortion performance on sensing data, prior approaches either require per-segment retraining incompatible with streaming, or have only been validated offline. None have been demonstrated end-to-end on a continuously streaming DAS acquisition system at scale. We present STeP-C (Spatio-Temporal Predictive Compression), a neural compression framework that decouples spatial encoding, temporal prediction, and entropy-optimized residual coding, trained end-to-end with a rate-distortion objective motivated by conditional entropy reduction. Critically, we identify entropy coding as the dominant bottleneck for streaming deployment. We address it through GPU-side symbol computation, cached probability tables, and parallel GIL-free arithmetic coding, together with FP16 inference and batched entropy coding, enabling a full real-time pipeline built around a GPU ring buffer. We validate this pipeline on a live DAS testbed, achieving a 98.85% file size reduction at 31.04 dB full-band PSNR and an average throughput of 535 MB/s, exceeding the 324 MB/s requirement for 1 kHz, 81 km DAS streams. We further show that STeP-C substantially outperforms conventional codecs at practical streaming bitrates, can be applied to unseen channel ranges within the same acquisition system without retraining, and largely maintains downstream detector consistency, with 96.62% high-confidence class agreement and 100% Jaccard similarity on detected event types.
blocks.zh: 分布式光纤感测(DFOS)技术如分布式声学感测(DAS)以超过每秒数百兆字节的速度生成连续高分辨率的时空数据,对实时存储和传输造成严重的挑战. 虽然神经压缩方法可以在感知数据上实现强烈的速率扭曲性能,但之前的方法要么要求每个区段的再培训与流化不兼容,要么只经过离线验证. 在不断流传的DAS采购系统上,没有任何一个端到端经过论证。 我们提出STeP-C(英语:Spatio-Temporal Presidentive Compression),是一种神经压缩框架,可以解开空间编码,时间预测,以及肽-优化的剩余编码,经过训练的端到端都具有以有条件的肽还原为动机的速率扭曲目标. 关键的是,我们确定 en编码是流派部署的主要瓶颈。 我们通过GPU侧符号计算,缓存概率表,和平行的GIL无算术编码,连同FP16推论和批量的 en编码来解决这个问题,使得能围绕GPU环缓冲器建造全实时管道. 我们在实时的DAS试验台上验证了这一管道,在31.04 dB全波段PSNR上实现了98.85%的文件尺寸削减,平均吞吐量为535 MB/s,超过了1千赫,81千米DAS流的324 MB/s要求. 我们进一步显示,STeP-C在实际流速比特率上大大超过常规的编码器,可以在不进行再培训的情况下应用到同一获取系统内的看不见的信道范围,并且基本上保持下游探测器的一致性,在检测到的事件类型上有96.62%的高自信级协议和100%的Jaccar相似性.

blocks.en: Distributed fiber-optic sensing (DFOS) has transformed large-scale environmental [ 16 ] and infrastructure [ 12 ] monitoring by enabling dense, continuous measurements along kilometer-scale cables. In particular, Distributed Acoustic Sensing (DAS) converts an existing fiber-optic cable into an array of thousands of spatially distributed vibration-sensing channels [ 28 ] , including cables already carrying live commercial traffic [ 27 ] , sampled at 500–1000 Hz, producing data volumes from tens of gigabytes to over a terabyte per hour. The resulting stream is naturally a two-dimensional “waterfall” image: one axis indexes position along the fiber, the other indexes time, and each pixel is a strain-rate measurement. Practitioners commonly inspect it through this plot, because coherent physical events appear as spatially and temporally extended visual structures, most visibly diagonal streaks whose slope encodes propagation velocity, see Figure 1 (b). Viewed this way, a DAS interrogator acts like a camera producing a temporally unbounded video of the ground. For applications such as seismic monitoring [ 1 ] , cable and pipeline intrusion detection [ 11 , 10 ] , traffic detection [ 27 , 14 ] , and subsea infrastructure monitoring [ 17 ] , the ability to compress and transmit or store this data in real time at acquisition is a critical operational requirement.
blocks.zh: 分布式光纤感测(DFOS)通过能够沿着千米级电缆进行密集连续测量,改变了大规模环境[16]和基础设施[12]监测。 特别是,分布式声波感应(DAS)将现有的光纤电缆转换成数以千计的空间分布式振动感应通道[28],包括已经搭载商业直播流量的电缆[27],取样时间为500-1 000。 Hz,生成数据卷 从几十千兆字节到超过一个千兆字节每小时。 由此形成的流自然是一个二维的"瀑布"图像:一个轴索引位置沿着纤维,另一个索引时间,每个像素都是一种菌株率的测量. 从业人员通常通过这一图案检查,因为连贯的物理事件似乎是空间和时间延伸的视觉结构,最明显的对角线,其坡度编码为传播速度,见图1(b)。 从这一角度来看,安全部的审讯人员表现得像摄像头,产生暂时没有限制的地面录像。 对于地震监测[1]、电缆和管道入侵探测[11、10]、交通探测[27、14]和海底基础设施监测[17]等应用,在获取数据时实时压缩和传输或储存这些数据的能力是一项关键的业务要求。

blocks.en:
The visual analogy is productive but not literal. Conventional image and
video codecs are designed primarily around natural-image and video
statistics and therefore do not directly match the structure of DAS
data. JPEG 2000 primarily exploits two-dimensional spatial redundancy,
while video codecs such as H.264 additionally use block-based temporal
prediction. In contrast, DAS exhibits strongly anisotropic structure:
neighboring sensing channels form a quasi-1D spatial sequence, while
temporal variation reflects smooth signal evolution punctuated by
localized propagating events rather than apparent object motion.
Moreover, DAS compression must preserve high-dynamic-range waveform
fidelity for downstream physical inference rather than primarily
perceptual visual quality. As we demonstrate experimentally, these
mismatches limit reconstruction fidelity at the low bitrates required
for practical streaming.
What transfers from vision is therefore not the codec but the paradigm: learned nonlinear transform coding with an entropy model [ 2 ] , and predictive residual coding across frames [ 6 , 18 ] , provided the transform, the predictor, and the entropy model are re-designed for the structure of the sensor data.

blocks.en: Existing DAS-specific compression methods address parts of this problem, but typically trade off compression efficiency, real-time operation, general-purpose reconstruction, or adaptability to continuous streams. These limitations leave a gap for a high-ratio neural compressor that can operate end-to-end on live DAS acquisition. In this work, we present STeP-C (Spatio-Temporal Predictive Compression), a neural compression framework for DFOS data whose overall workflow is illustrated in Figure 1 . STeP-C achieves competitive rate-distortion performance through a modular three-stage architecture: (1) a 1D convolutional spatial encoder; (2) a recurrent temporal predictor that forecasts the next latent frame from past embeddings; and (3) an entropy-optimized residual encoder trained under a learned entropy model.
blocks.zh: 现有的针对DAS的压缩方法解决了部分这个问题,但一般是用压缩效率,实时操作,通用重建,或对连续流的适应性来交换. 这些限制为高射神经压缩机留下了一个缺口,可以在DAS直播获取上运行端到端. 在这项工作中,我们介绍了STeP-C(Spatio-Temporal Presidentive Compression),这是一个DFOS数据的神经压缩框架,其总体工作流程如图1所示. STeP-C通过模块化的三相架构实现竞争性速率扭曲性能:(1)1D演化空间编码器;(2)从过去的嵌入中预测下一个潜伏框架的经常性时间预测器;(3)在学习的 en模型下训练的 en-优化残余编码器.

blocks.en: Each stage is the sensor-domain analogue of a component in learned video compression: the 1D convolutional spatial encoder plays the role of the intra-frame analysis transform, replacing 2D convolutions with convolutions along the fiber’s channel dimension; the recurrent temporal predictor replaces optical-flow motion compensation, forecasting the next latent directly rather than warping a reference frame; and the residual encoder performs residual coding under a learned entropy model. The temporal predictor is motivated by conditional entropy reduction: conditioning the current latent on available temporal context cannot increase its uncertainty, and reduces it when the current latent is statistically dependent on that context. DAS signals typically exhibit strong temporal correlation, motivating predictive coding before residual entropy coding (see Sec. 3.1 ).
blocks.zh: 每个阶段都是学习视频压缩中一个组件的传感器-域模拟:1D演化空间编码器发挥机身内侧分析变换的作用,沿纤维的通道维度用转动取代2D演化;经常时间预测器取代光学流动补偿,预测下一个潜伏直接而不是扭曲一个参考框架;剩余编码器在学习的演化模型下进行剩余编码. 时间预测器的动机是有条件的递减:将当前潜伏因素限定在现有时间背景上无法增加其不确定性,当当前潜伏因素在统计学上依赖于这一背景时,则可以减少不确定性。 DAS信号一般表现出很强的时间相关性,在剩余 en编码之前激发预测编码(见Sec. 3.1)。

blocks.en: To translate this into deployable real-time throughput, we identify entropy coding as the dominant bottleneck and redesign its implementation for streaming operation. Symbol computation is moved to the GPU, probability tables are cached across calls, and arithmetic coding is parallelized across GIL-free C++ threads, together yielding a 30× speedup over the unoptimized baseline. We validate the resulting pipeline not in simulation alone, but on a live DAS testbed with 81,000 sensing channels, corresponding to approximately 81 km of fiber at 1 m channel spacing, achieving 87.30× compression and 31.04 dB full-band PSNR at an average throughput of 535 MB/s. Beyond the live testbed, we evaluate reconstruction on fiber channels not seen during training and assess whether a downstream event detector produces consistent predictions on compressed reconstructions relative to the original data.
blocks.zh: 为了将这一点转化为可部署的实时吞吐量,我们确定“entropy Coding”是主要的瓶颈,并重新设计其实施流程操作。 符号计算被移动到GPU,概率表被缓存到调用之间,算术编码被平行到GIL自由的C++线条之间,共同产生30×比未优化基线的速度. 我们不仅通过模拟,而且通过81,000个感应通道的实时DAS测试台验证由此产生的管道,相当于1米信道间距约81公里的纤维,以535 MB/s的平均吞吐量达到87.30x压缩和31.04 dB全波段PSNR。 除了现场试验台之外,我们评价在训练期间没有看到的纤维通道上的重建,并评估下游事件探测器相对于原始数据是否对压缩重建产生一致的预测。

blocks.en:
Our main contributions are: • Vision-centric formulation for DFOS compression. We model the DAS waterfall as a spatio-temporal visual signal and adapt
learned transform coding to its 1D spatial layout and high-dynamic-range
statistics, with a modular architecture separating spatial encoding,
temporal prediction, and residual coding. • Real-time neural compression system. We identify entropy coding as the dominant throughput bottleneck and redesign the coding path with GPU-side symbol computation, cached probability tables, parallel GIL-free arithmetic coding, FP16 inference, and batched coding. The resulting system enables, to our knowledge, the first neural DAS compressor validated end-to-end in a live acquisition pipeline directly coupled to a continuously streaming DAS interrogator. • Validation on real deployments. We outperform conventional and DAS-specific codecs, demonstrate reconstruction beyond the training channel range without retraining, and show that downstream detector predictions remain largely consistent after compression.

blocks.en: STeP-C extends neural compression beyond its conventional image and video settings to a domain-specific but task-agnostic streaming problem. Rather than transferring an existing visual codec, we adapt the underlying principles of learned transform coding, temporal prediction, residual entropy coding, and rate-distortion optimization to the distinct spatial and temporal regularities of DFOS data. This formulation preserves a general-purpose reconstruction rather than optimizing the representation for a predefined downstream task, allowing the compressed signal to support storage, transmission, visualization, and future analyses. More broadly, STeP-C demonstrates that learned predictive and entropy coding can exploit structured redundancy beyond natural-image statistics, while its real-time deployment exposes practical bottlenecks, particularly entropy-coding throughput and host–device transfer overhead, that are often hidden in offline evaluation. These observations may also inform neural compression systems for other large-scale, continuously streamed sensing data. Table 1 summarizes how representative DAS data compression approaches compare along the deployment-oriented criteria discussed below.
blocks.zh: STeP-C将其常规图像和视频设置之外的神经压缩扩展到一个特定域但任务不可知的流体问题. 与其转移现有的可视编码器,不如将所学变换编码,时间预测,剩余演算编码,速率扭曲优化等根本原则,适应DFOS数据独特的时空规律. 这种提法保留了一般用途的重建,而不是优化预定义的下游任务的表示,使压缩的信号能够支持存储,传输,可视化,以及未来的分析. 更广泛地说,STeP-C表明,所学的预测和entropy编码可以在自然图像统计之外利用结构上的冗余,而其实时部署则暴露出实际瓶颈,特别是Entropy-coding吞吐量和主机-device传输管理费用,这些往往隐藏在离线评价中。 这些观测还可能为其他大规模连续流传的遥感数据的神经压缩系统提供信息. 表1总结了具有代表性的DAS数据压缩方法如何按照下文讨论的面向部署的标准进行比较。

blocks.en: 2.1 Neural Image and Video Compression
blocks.zh: 2.1 神经图像和视频压缩

blocks.en: End-to-end learned compression has achieved state-of-the-art rate-distortion performance on natural images and video. [ 2 ] introduced the hyperprior framework using nonlinear transforms and learned entropy models. For video, [ 18 ] proposed DVC using optical flow for motion estimation, while [ 6 ] proposed inter-frame neural compression using residual coding in the feature space. [ 20 ] extended this with joint autoregressive and hierarchical priors. Multiple-frame prediction was explored by [ 15 , 5 ] . STeP-C adapts the residual latent coding paradigm from these works to the DFOS domain, replacing 2D image encoders with 1D convolutional encoders suited for fiber-optic sensor arrays. Unlike the methods above, which are typically evaluated on pre-recorded video, the proposed method explicitly addresses the throughput constraints of compressing a live sensor stream in real time.
blocks.zh: 端到端的学习压缩在自然影像和视频上实现了最先进的速率扭曲性能. [2]采用非线性变换和学习的 en模型引入了超前框架. 对于视频,[18]提议使用光学流进行运动估计的DVC,而[6]则提议使用特征空间的剩余编码进行机体间神经压缩. [20] 扩展了它与联合自动和等级前科。 [15, 5]探讨了多重框架预测。 STeP-C将这些作品的剩余潜在编码范式调整为DFOS域,将2D图像编码器替换为适合光纤传感器阵列的1D转录编码器. 与上述通常在预录视频上评价的方法不同,拟议方法明确解决实时压缩直播传感器流的吞吐量限制.

blocks.en: 2.2 Neural and Task-Oriented Compression Methods for DAS
blocks.zh: 2.2 DAS的神经和任务定位压缩方法

blocks.en: Learned models have been applied directly to DAS compression, but under assumptions incompatible with streaming. Wang et al. [ 25 ] evaluate a recurrent autoencoder on pre-recorded DAS segments, without demonstrating continuous real-time compression. Chen et al. [ 4 ] compress 2D patches with a vision transformer, reaching ratios near 50× when combined with downsampling, but train self-supervised per segment: each new 60-second window requires on the order of 30 minutes of GPU training, or roughly 10 fine-tuning iterations with transfer from a previous window. This suits archival compression of recorded campaigns but not a live stream, where a fixed model must generalize across incoming data without retraining. Shen et al. [ 23 ] instead map a frequency-band-energy extractor into the compressed-sensing domain, detecting and classifying events at a 70% reduction in transmitted data without reconstructing the signal; this is fast for the task it targets but produces no reusable data for storage, transmission, or analyses not anticipated at acquisition time.
blocks.zh: 学到的模型被直接应用于DAS压缩,但在与流线不兼容的假设下. 王等编. [25] 在预先录制的DAS片段上评价一个经常性自动编码器,而不显示连续的实时压缩. 陈等. [4]将2D补丁压缩为视觉变压器,在与下采样结合时达到接近50×的比例,但每段的列车自控:每个新的60秒窗口需要大约30分钟的GPU训练,或者用前一个窗口的转动进行约10个微调的迭代. 这适合对已记录的运动进行档案压缩,但不适合现场直播,因为固定模式必须在不进行再培训的情况下,将输入的数据普遍化。 沈等编著. [23] 相反,将一个频带能量提取器映射到压缩传感器域,在不重建信号的情况下,在传输数据减少70%的情况下检测和分类事件;这对于它所要完成的任务来说是快的,但不能产生可重复使用的数据,用于存储,传输,或者在获取时无法预期的分析.

blocks.en: 2.3 Non-Neural Compression for DAS
blocks.zh: 2.3 DAS的非神经压缩

blocks.en: Non-neural DAS compressors provide an important deployment baseline because several already support real-time operation without model training. Dong et al. [ 7 ] integrate lossless compression directly into the DAS storage workflow, demonstrating compression at acquisition rate. DASPack [ 22 ] combines wavelet transforms and linear prediction with arithmetic entropy coding, providing lossless or bounded-error reconstruction while remaining suitable for real-time CPU deployment. Sun et al. [ 24 ] similarly employ asymmetric numeral systems (ANS) entropy coding for high-ratio DAS compression. These approaches demonstrate that explicit entropy-coded bitstreams and real-time processing are achievable with non-neural pipelines, while relying on hand-designed transforms and predictors rather than learned spatio-temporal representations. STeP-C targets a different operating point by combining learned predictive coding with entropy coding, general-purpose reconstruction, and real-time operation.
blocks.zh: 非神经式DAS压缩机提供了重要的部署基线,因为有几台已经支持没有模型训练的实时操作. 董等编. [7]将无损失压缩直接整合到DAS存储工作流程中,以获取率显示压缩. DASPack [22] 将波形变换和线性预测与算术素编码相结合,提供无损或有界-误差重建,同时仍然适合实时CPU部署. 孙等. blocks.en: 2.4 From Real-Time Inference to Live Streaming Deployment
blocks.zh: 2.4 从实时推论到现场流动部署

blocks.en:
Real-time capability has been explored at different stages of the DAS processing pipeline, but fast inference alone does not establish that a neural compressor can operate continuously at the acquisition rate. Ni et al. [ 21 ] , for example, demonstrate that their lightweight reconstruction model can run on a Raspberry Pi, showing the feasibility of neural processing at the edge. Their evaluation, however, benchmarks reconstruction from subsampled DAS data rather than an end-to-end compression pipeline directly coupled to a live interrogator. Classical methods such as Dong et al. [ 7 ] and DASPack [ 22 ] do demonstrate real-time DAS compression, but learned approaches have largely been evaluated on pre-recorded data or through component-level runtime measurements. For continuous neural compression, the complete acquisition-to-bitstream pipeline must keep pace with incoming data while handling buffering, preprocessing, encoding, and output without interrupting the stream.
To our knowledge, STeP-C is the first neural DAS compressor validated under this end-to-end live-acquisition setting.

在DAS处理管道的不同阶段探索了实时能力,但仅靠快速推论并不能确定神经压缩机能够以获取速度持续运行. 例如Ni 等人 [21] 证明了他们的轻量级重建模型可以运行在Raspberry Pi上,显示了在边缘进行神经处理的可行性. 然而,他们的评价是根据对DAS数据进行分样的重建基准,而不是直接与现场讯问相结合的端到端压缩管道。 诸如董等人[7]和DASPack[22]等古典方法确实展示了实时DAS压缩,但学到的方法基本上通过预先录制的数据或通过组件级别的运行时间测量得到了评价. 对于持续的神经压缩,完整的获取到比特流管道必须在处理缓冲,预处理,编码和输出的同时,与收到的数据保持同步,而不会中断流.
据我们所知,STeP-C是第一个在这个端到端的直播获取设置下验证的神经DAS压缩机.

blocks.en: 3.2 Real-Time Systems Engineering
blocks.zh: 3.2 实时系统工程

blocks.en: Identifying the bottleneck. A trained STeP-C model is only deployable in real time if every stage of the pipeline sustains the target throughput. We find that the spatial encoder, temporal predictor, and residual network all run efficiently on the GPU and do not limit throughput. Instead, entropy coding becomes the primary bottleneck. Standard arithmetic coding implementations, including the one provided by CompressAI [ 3 ] , exhibit several inefficiencies in a streaming setting. The coder holds Python’s Global Interpreter Lock during execution, so only one thread can run at a time even when calls are issued asynchronously. The probability table, expressed as a cumulative distribution function (CDF), is recomputed from float32 to int16 on every single call, even though the underlying model has not changed. Quantized symbols are computed by subtracting medians on the CPU, requiring a device-to-host transfer of the full latent tensor before the subtraction can occur. Coding also proceeds sequentially per element, with no parallelism across the batch.

blocks.en: An optimized entropy-coding path. We address these inefficiencies with a custom C++ extension that reorganizes the entropy-coding path around several complementary optimizations. Symbol computation moves to the GPU: medians are subtracted from quantized values directly on-device, before any data is transferred to the CPU, eliminating a redundant round trip across the PCIe bus. The CDF table is cached: the conversion from float32 to int16 happens once, at model load or update time, and every subsequent call reuses it. The extension releases Python’s GIL and performs arithmetic coding across multiple GIL-free C++ threads (8 in our deployment), enabling true parallelism across the batch. Together, these changes yield a 30× improvement in encoding throughput over the unoptimized pipeline. We apply two further accelerations on top of this fix: running the spatial encoder, temporal predictor, and residual MLP in float16 under mixed-precision autocast to reduce neural inference cost on supported hardware, and batching entropy coding across all time steps in a sequence, issuing a single coder call per batch rather than one call per time step. Section 4.5 reports the cumulative throughput gains from these optimizations.

CDF表是缓存的:从浮点32到int16的转换发生一次,在模型加载或更新时间,之后的每一个调用都会重复使用. 扩展会释放 Python 的 GIL , 并跨多个无 GIL 的 C++ 线程进行算术编码( 在我们的部署中为 8) , 从而在整个批次实现真正的平行 。 这些变化加在一起使编码吞吐量比未优化的管道有30×改进。 我们在这个固定点上再加两个加速度:在混合精度自动播报下运行空间编码器、时间预测器和浮点16中的剩余MLP,以减少辅助硬件的神经推导成本;按顺序分批分解所有时间步骤的Entropy编码,每批发出一个编码器调用,而不是每个时间步发出一个调用。 第4.5节报告了这些优化的累积吞吐量收益。

blocks.en: Pipeline architecture . Sustaining real-time throughput on a continuously arriving sensor stream requires an acquisition-aware streaming pipeline, as illustrated in Figure 3 . We implement two concurrent processes that communicate through GPU shared memory. The acquisition process interfaces directly with the DAS interrogator, receiving raw phase frames at the full acquisition rate across all channels, and performs three tasks concurrently: writing raw frames to disk for archival (optional), writing each row into a GPU ring buffer, and incrementing a write counter in shared memory. The ring buffer holds 8,192 slots, providing approximately 8 seconds of buffering headroom, and is shared with the compression process via a CUDA interprocess communication (IPC) handle, avoiding CPU staging of the data. The compression process monitors the write counter with a lightweight polling thread, consumes new rows directly from the ring buffer via a GPU-to-GPU copy, and applies, in sequence, a streaming band-pass filter, normalization, spatial patch extraction, neural compression, and parallel entropy coding, before writing compressed output. Two of these steps require modification from their offline counterparts to remain correct under streaming. The band-pass filter is stateful, so applying it independently to each incoming chunk introduces edge artifacts at chunk boundaries; we carry the filter state across chunks by prepending the final rows of each chunk to the next as warm-up context. Normalization uses a hyperbolic tangent transform with a fixed 99th-percentile scale established offline during training, so that scaling remains consistent across chunks rather than depending on the statistics of each chunk in isolation.

blocks.en:
Datasets. We evaluate on three real-world DAS datasets collected using our system.
The NJ Coastal Fiber Array (NJCFA) consists of 40 recordings from
a fiber-optic cable deployment along the New Jersey coast, each containing
3,584 sensing channels. We segment the recordings into sequences of T T consecutive frames, with each frame spanning 512 channels, yielding 22,281
training samples and 5,565 validation samples, together with a held-out test
set of 27,916 samples. NJCFA is used for rate-distortion evaluation, comparison with
conventional and DAS-specific codecs, and architecture ablations.
The Dallas Ambient DAS (DADAS) dataset consists of continuous recordings
collected from an urban fiber deployment in Dallas at 800 Hz across 81,000
channels. We use a 4,000-channel sub-band (channels 6,000–10,000), yielding 73,472 training samples, 18,368 validation samples, and 89,908 test samples. DADAS is used to evaluate rate-distortion performance, qualitative reconstruction, transfer to fiber channels outside the training range, and downstream detector consistency. For both NJCFA and DADAS, training, validation, and test sets are formed from separate recordings acquired at different times; no recording is shared across splits.
The Princeton Fiber Testbed (PFT) consists of data streamed directly
from a live DAS interrogator at 1,000 Hz across 81,000 channels. PFT is used
to evaluate the complete real-time compression pipeline under live acquisition,
including end-to-end throughput, compression ratio, and full-band reconstruction
quality.

We train four model variants, STeP-C-tiny, small, medium, and large, with residual latent dimensions z = 32 , 64 , 128 , z=32,64,128, and 256 256 , respectively. Unless otherwise noted, training and evaluation use sequences of T = 10 T=10 consecutive DAS frames, with each frame spanning 512 sensing channels. Training uses the Adam optimizer [ 13 ] with the rate-distortion objective described in Section 3.1 , with λ r = 0.001 \lambda_{r}=0.001 , λ d = 1 \lambda_{d}=1 , and λ tp = 0.1 \lambda_{\mathrm{tp}}=0.1 . All experiments run on an NVIDIA RTX 6000 Ada GPU (48 GB) and AMD Threadripper PRO 7965WX CPU. Preprocessing follows Section 3.2 . For data preprocessing, NJCFA data undergo phase unwrapping followed by a 5 Hz Chebyshev Type I high-pass filter to remove low-frequency background drift. DADAS and PFT data are band-pass filtered from 1 to 200 Hz and normalized using a tanh transform with a fixed 99th-percentile scale. For streaming deployment, the band-pass filter is applied statefully: the final rows of each chunk are prepended to the next as warm-up history, eliminating edge artifacts that arise when filtering each incoming window independently.

blocks.en: Figure 5 (a) reports the rate-distortion performance of STeP-C variants on NJCFA and DADAS. Across both datasets, increasing the residual latent dimension z z improves reconstruction quality at the cost of higher BPS, providing a consistent capacity-rate-distortion trade-off across model variants. On NJCFA, STeP-C-small achieves 34.51 dB at 0.436 BPS, while on DADAS the same model variant reaches 41.13 dB at 0.424 BPS. The higher PSNR observed on DADAS at comparable bitrates reflects differences in the signal statistics of the two datasets, while the overall trend remains consistent across deployments.

blocks.en: 4.3 Comparison with Conventional Codecs
blocks.zh: 4.3 与常规编码的比较

blocks.en:
Figure 5 (b) compares the rate-distortion performance of STeP-C with JPEG 2000, H.264, MP3, DASPack [ 22 ] , and EnCodec [ 8 ] on NJCFA. STeP-C provides operating points below 0.5 BPS while maintaining comparatively high reconstruction quality. At 0.436 BPS, STeP-C achieves 34.51 dB PSNR. EnCodec is the only other method evaluated below 0.5 BPS, but its PSNR remains near 32 dB across the tested bitrate range. DASPack operates over a relatively narrow bitrate range of approximately 1.1–1.5 BPS, with reconstruction quality increasing sharply across its tested operating points, but it does not cover the sub-0.5 BPS regime. At its lowest tested bitrate, H.264 reaches 27.03 dB at 0.68 BPS, more than 7 dB below STeP-C despite using a higher bitrate. JPEG 2000 does not produce an operating point below 1.80 BPS in our evaluation, where it achieves 33.61 dB, while STeP-C reaches 37.48 dB at 1.01 BPS. MP3 achieves 28.62 dB at 1.10 BPS and remains below STeP-C over the evaluated range.
In the practical low-bitrate regime below 0.5 BPS, STeP-C is the only evaluated method that operates in this regime while maintaining high reconstruction fidelity.

blocks.en: 4.5 Real-Time Throughput
blocks.zh: 4.5 实时流量

blocks.en: We first evaluate compression throughput in a simulated streaming setting, where pre-recorded DAS data are supplied to the compression pipeline at controlled rates. This isolates the computational throughput of the compressor from live acquisition and file handling overhead. Figure 7 summarizes the cumulative throughput gains achieved by each optimization applied to STeP-C-small model. The unoptimized baseline using CompressAI’s standard arithmetic coder achieves only 13 MB/s on encoding, far below the 324 MB/s real-time requirement. The custom entropy coder alone raises this to 392 MB/s, a 30× speedup. Adding FP16 mixed-precision inference raises encoding to 604 MB/s. Batching entropy coding across time steps reaches 647 MB/s. The 30 × \times gain from the custom coder identifies standard entropy coding as the primary bottleneck in the unoptimized pipeline, while FP16 inference and batched coding provide additional throughput gains once this bottleneck is removed.

blocks.en: 4.6 Live Testbed Evaluation
blocks.zh: 4.6 现场测试床评价

blocks.en:
We next evaluate STeP-C on the PFT dataset under live acquisition. Unlike the simulated streaming evaluation in Section 4.5 , this experiment measures the complete pipeline while data are continuously acquired from a DAS interrogator. The model is trained on a 256-channel sub-band and then applied without retraining to one hour of streamed data, comprising 1,111 consecutively acquired files of 3,240 time frames each, sampled at 1 kHz across 81,000 channels.
Across the full acquisition, STeP-C compresses 1.166 TB of raw DAS data to 13.36 GB, corresponding to an 87.30 × \times compression ratio and a 98.85% reduction in file size at 0.367 BPS. Reconstruction on the trained sub-band reaches 33.64 dB PSNR, while full-band reconstruction achieves 31.04 dB. The model therefore remains usable across the full acquisition footprint without channel-specific retraining, though reconstruction quality degrades measurably outside the trained channel range. Including streaming preprocessing, neural compression, parallel entropy coding, and file I/O, the end-to-end live pipeline achieves an average processing throughput of 535 MB/s over the live acquisition, exceeding the 324 MB/s throughput required for 1,000 Hz acquisition across 81,000 channels, with no dropped acquisition frames during the evaluated run.

blocks.en: 4.7 Downstream Detector Consistency
blocks.zh: 4.7 下游探测器一致性

blocks.en:
We assess the impact of compression on the DADAS dataset using a consistency-based protocol in which the same pre-trained detector [ 10 ] is applied independently to the original and reconstructed data. Before detector inference, both streams undergo the same detector-specific preprocessing. We invert the tanh
normalization, apply the detector’s temporal filtering, and aggregate every 30 consecutive samples by averaging their absolute amplitudes. Quantitative results are summarized in Table 3 . Figure 8 provides qualitative examples showing that representative event patterns remain visually consistent after reconstruction and lead to the same detector outputs. Across all event windows, the overall top-1 and top-5 class agreements are 83.01 % 83.01\% and 98.72 % 98.72\% , respectively. Restricting the comparison to high-confidence predictions ( p ≥ 0.6 p\geq 0.6 ) increases top-1 agreement to 96.62 % 96.62\% , showing substantially higher consistency among confident detector outputs. The corresponding prediction scores remain strongly correlated ( r = 0.851 r=0.851 ), with a mean probability deviation of 0.079 0.079 . Per-class top-1 and top-5 agreements for the six most frequent event classes are shown in Figure 9 (a), while Figure 9 (b) shows the corresponding top-1 confusion matrix. Using the same confidence threshold for event detection, the reconstructed data produce 92.13 % 92.13\% as many detections as the original, while the set of detected event classes remains unchanged, yielding a Jaccard similarity of 100 % 100\% . These results indicate that STeP-C largely preserves the pretrained detector’s output behavior, including high-confidence predictions and the set of event categories identified from the original data.

blocks.en: 5 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 5 结论

blocks.en: We presented STeP-C, a neural compression framework for DAS data, and demonstrated its end-to-end deployment under live acquisition. The system achieves an average throughput of 535 MB/s with 87.30 × \times compression on continuously streamed interrogator data and 31.04 dB full-band PSNR. Across offline evaluations, STeP-C provides favorable rate-distortion performance in the low-bitrate regime, while temporal prediction consistently reduces the bitrate required for a given reconstruction quality. Downstream evaluation further shows strong consistency between detector outputs on original and reconstructed data, reaching 96.62% high-confidence class agreement and 100% Jaccard similarity over detected event classes. These results demonstrate that learned predictive compression can support high-ratio, real-time DAS streaming while retaining both reconstruction quality and downstream utility. Future work will explore spatial representations that generalize more uniformly across fiber locations and extend downstream validation to additional tasks such as event localization and arrival-time picking.
